examples.7.1 Scope and content plan: Moonshift ships with six rooms and twelve shifts on PC and tablet, plus English-only text. Air routing, cargo placement, and the shift timer are Must; radio narrative is Should; room decoration is Could and the second biome is Won't. If week 24 slips, the team cuts room decoration and ships four rooms, twelve shifts, and eighty radio lines.
examples.7.2 Milestones and schedule: Concept passed in week 2 with a three-reference pitch, and the week 6 prototype needs a ten-minute graybox plus five external testers. The vertical slice lands week 12, alpha week 24 with six rooms playable, beta week 32 with zero S1/S2 bugs, and launch week 36. A 15% buffer sits after each phase, and the critical path runs through save/load, the room pipeline, and tablet performance.
examples.7.3 Team and responsibilities: Four part-time people carry Moonshift: Ana Rivera as 0.5 creative director, Mateo Chen as designer and narrative, Jon Okafor as programmer, Sana Patel as artist, and Lina Novak as 0.5 producer and audio lead. The producer owns schedule and appendices, the designer owns gameplay and narrative, and the programmer holds the certification waiver. QA and marketing stay contracted, with the producer reviewing every vendor package.
examples.7.4 Budget and outsourcing: The production budget is $66,000: $54,000 personnel, $2,000 art and audio, $900 software, $1,200 dev kits, $400 QA and certification, $1,500 marketing, and $6,000 contingency. The art package buys forty props, one hero character, and eight music tracks; the trailer is a separate 60-second contract paid 30/30/30/10. Monthly burn is $7,300 during the nine-month build, and a separate $22,000 reserve covers three months past launch.
examples.7.5 Risk register: Shift 4 is the top risk at Medium/High: playtesters stall for three minutes or more, so the designer runs room 4 every Friday and adds a skip after three failures. Touch input is second at Medium/High, with the programmer shipping a tablet prototype in week 2 and grid snapping only. Art scope stays High/High; the artist reuses six room shells and cancels the second biome.
examples.7.6 QA and playtesting: Every Friday the team runs a 30-minute internal playtest, and every two weeks five players aged 9–12 test the current build with guardian consent. In the May 14 build, four of five players skipped the tutorial card, so the designer moved the airlock prompt inline and scheduled a re-test for 28 May. The pass bar is five of six testers finishing unaided; S1 bugs get fixed within 24 hours.
examples.7.7 Certification and compliance: Moonshift targets ESRB E, PEGI 3, and USK 0; CERO A is deferred because Japanese localization is not in the launch budget. The compliance checklist covers suspend/resume, controller disconnect, save icon, and offline boot, with the producer owning the platform submission. The store page states no loot boxes, no purchases, and no online chat, and the privacy policy names a 30-day deletion contact.
examples.7.8 Marketing and launch: Moonshift launches at $14.99 on PC and tablet with a free two-shift demo whose save carries into the full game. The 60-second trailer opens on a dead airlock, shows three repairs by 30 seconds, and ends on the week 36 release date and wishlist link. The T-90 checklist starts the store page and wishlist campaign, with press and creator keys out at T-30.
examples.7.9 Post-launch and live operations: After launch, Moonshift gets a 48-hour hotfix for blockers, then patches only for verified defects; the first patch lands at T+7. There are zero seasons: at 20,000 copies the team builds a six-shift expansion at $4.99, otherwise it ships a final offline patch and archives the store page. Telemetry is reviewed weekly for 90 days, and the postmortem lands at T+30.
